request.prompt:
You are an independent evaluation judge. Grade the proposed remedy, not the
writing style of this prompt. A good remedy changes a concrete future behavior,
is broad enough to cover the failure mode without becoming a platitude, uses a
real `Use when ...` trigger when it is a skill, leaks no evidence-specific
project nouns into the remedy text, and uses the cheapest adequate remedy type.

Score every dimension from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). Give exactly one concise
sentence of justification for each score. Do not infer facts that are absent.

PROPOSAL:
{
  "failure_statement": "Instructions were missed.",
  "remedy_content": {
    "target": "global",
    "text": "Always carefully follow instructions and do high quality work."
  },
  "remedy_type": "claude-md",
  "routing_rationale": "A rule may help."
}

response.result: {"actionability":{"score":1,"justification":"The text \"Always carefully follow instructions and do high quality work\" prescribes no concrete, checkable behavior change — it's advice everyone already knows to follow."},"generality_without_vagueness":{"score":1,"justification":"It is pure platitude with no distinguishing content: it applies to literally every task and thus constrains nothing about the specific failure mode."},"trigger_quality":{"score":1,"justification":"There is no real trigger condition — it's injected as an always-on global instruction rather than a scoped \"Use when ...\" rule tied to any identifiable circumstance."},"leakage":{"score":5,"justification":"The remedy text contains no project-specific nouns or evidence details, so there is no leakage risk, though this is only because the text says nothing substantive at all."},"routing_fitness":{"score":1,"justification":"Permanently adding a vague blanket rule to global CLAUDE.md is disproportionate and not the cheapest adequate response to an underspecified failure statement (\"Instructions were missed\") that gives no mechanism to fix."}}

actionability.justification: The text "Always carefully follow instructions and do high quality work" prescribes no concrete, checkable behavior change — it's advice everyone already knows to follow.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: It is pure platitude with no distinguishing content: it applies to literally every task and thus constrains nothing about the specific failure mode.

leakage.justification: The remedy text contains no project-specific nouns or evidence details, so there is no leakage risk, though this is only because the text says nothing substantive at all.

routing_fitness.justification: Permanently adding a vague blanket rule to global CLAUDE.md is disproportionate and not the cheapest adequate response to an underspecified failure statement ("Instructions were missed") that gives no mechanism to fix.

trigger_quality.justification: There is no real trigger condition — it's injected as an always-on global instruction rather than a scoped "Use when ..." rule tied to any identifiable circumstance.
